complexity.notes: The recursion is correct but redundant: maxDepth re-walks each subtree once per ancestor, which is what pushes the running time to O(n log n) on balanced trees and O(n^2) on skewed ones. A single bottom-up pass that ||returns each subtree's height while updating a running best of left_height + right_height|| reaches O(n) time. Minor style: `max([...])` builds a throwaway list where `max(a, b, c)` would do, and the if/else in diameterOfBinaryTree could just be a guard clause.
complexity.summary: At every node, computes the height of both subtrees with a separate maxDepth traversal, takes their sum as a candidate diameter, and recurses into both subtrees to take the overall max. Heights are recomputed from scratch at each node rather than reused.
